pageCache.pageTitle: New King's Road School, London. Part of the Quality First Education Trust. - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Our School » Welcome
Thank you for taking the time to visit our school website. I am incredibly proud to be Head Teacher of this wonderful community school. New King's Road School (formerly Thomas's Academy) is a values-led school and we have built our school upon the following values:
‘Be Kind’ – Belonging, Excellence, Kindness, Integrity, Never Give Up, and Diversity.
Our Curriculum Statement LEARN drives our curriculum decisions for our learners to be engaging, ambitious, relevant and nurturing. We develop positive attitudes to learning throughout the school. From the youngest classes and throughout the school, we teach the children what it means to be "Excellent Learners."
We encourage families to visit us to learn more about the school. We have a regular weekly tour on Wednesday mornings. To find out more and book your place, please visit our School Tours page.
We look forward to welcoming you to New King's Road School.

Extra-Curricular Activities
For Our Parents/Carers » Extra-Curricular Activities
We are proud to provide an exciting and broad curriculum for our pupils. During school hours, pupils have opportunities to access lots of extra curricular activities including our outdoor learning programme, swimming and dance. In addition, children have many wider experiences including trips, Bikeability, gardening in our school garden, the Year 4 sleepover, the Year 5 and 6 residential, visitors to the school, and access to sports competitions. We have many whole school events throughout the year including World Book Day, Walk to School Week, our annual Easter Egg Hunt, Neurodiversity Week and many more.

We also offer a wide range of after-school clubs for children at New King's Road School that children can access once they are in Reception. Some clubs are run by our internal staff and some by outside agencies. Examples include:

pageCache.pageTitle: New King's Road School, London. Part of the Quality First Education Trust. - Breakfast and After-School Care
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After-School Care
For Our Parents/Carers » Breakfast and After-School Care
Wraparound care is available term time, all year round. This is managed and run by the school and can be booked using the Teachers2parents app.
Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club is offered at £3.50 per day and can be attended on an ad hoc basis. This takes place in the lower hall where children will be served breakfast. Games will be on offer for the children to play with then they will go to class at 8.45am. Please book no later than the night before the day of attendance.
Shine Bright - After-School Club
Our after-school club, Shine Bright, is offered at £10 per day until 4.30pm, £15 per day until 5.30pm and £18 per day until 6pm. It can be attended on an ad hoc basis and should be booked no later than the night before the day of attendance. Shine Bright does not run on the last day of each full term (December, April and July) when the children finish early at 2pm.
You can pay for your after-school care via Childcare Vouchers or Tax Free Childcare. Please contact the School Office to arrange this.

pageCache.pageTitle: New King's Road School, London. Part of the Quality First Education Trust. - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Our Learning » Music
At New King's Road School, we follow The Kapow Primary Music scheme which is designed to help pupils recognise themselves as musical and to nurture a lifelong love of music.
The scheme develops the skills, knowledge, and understanding needed to become confident performers, composers, and listeners. The curriculum introduces pupils to music from across the world, encouraging respect and appreciation for the music of all traditions and communities.
Pupils build musical skills through singing, playing tuned and untuned instruments, improvising, composing and listening and responding to music. They develop an understanding of the historical and cultural context of the music they encounter and learn how music can be notated.
The scheme also supports the development of transferable skills, including teamwork, leadership, creative thinking, problem-solving, decision-making and presentation and performance abilities. These skills are integral to pupils’ development as learners and have wide application in their lives beyond school.
The Five Strands
The National curriculum organises the attainment targets for Music under:
Accordingly, Kapow Primary’s Music curriculum has been structured with these strands running through each unit. The strands ensure balanced coverage of the different areas of Music and that both substantive and disciplinary aspects are covered.

pageCache.pageTitle: New King's Road School, London. Part of the Quality First Education Trust. - Attendance
pageCache.text:
Attendance
For Our Parents/Carers » Attendance
School attendance is very important to make sure that every child reaches their full potential not only academically but also socially and emotionally. We expect all children to attend school every day and to be in the playground at the start of the day. Periods of absence and poor punctuality are disruptive to the children’s learning and send poor messages about the value of education. We ask parents and carers to support us in ensuring their children do not miss out through unnecessary absences.
All pupils’ attendance and punctuality is monitored. Any child who attends school less than 90% of the time is considered to be a Persistent Absentee and a referral to Educational Welfare will be made for them.
Further information can be found in the Department for Education's Working together to improve school attendance guidance, and our Attendance Policy.
Holidays
Holidays are expected to be taken during the school holidays and parents do not have a right to take their child(ren) out of school for holidays during term time. Exceptions may be made at the discretion of the Headteacher. All requests for absence are treated sympathetically and only in exceptional circumstances will they be approved. A Leave of Absence form should be completed in the case of any request for leave, including holidays and is available from the school office. Holidays during term time are not allowed and will be classified as unauthorised.
Collection Arrangements
It is essential that the school knows if there is any change in collection arrangements for your child. Staff are available in the playground at the start and end of each day for you to talk to. Please ring the School Office on 020 7736 2318 before 2.30pm If there are any last minute changes, e.g. someone other than the person known to staff is to collect your child at the end of the day. Calling before 2.30pm is important as it allows time for us to get messages to classrooms before the end of the day.
Punctuality
All late arrivals to school must report to the School Office. Failure to do so means that your child will remain absent on the school register and in the event of an emergency would be considered as absent. It could also mean that your child will not be included in the school meal numbers for the day.
Absences
If you know your child will be late or absent, for example due to a hospital appointment or school visit, please provide the office with the relevant appointment letter in advance of the absence. Letters regarding absence should be handed in to the office and not the class teacher. This will enable us to keep all documentation regarding your child’s absences on file. Where possible, please make essential appointments after registration in the afternoon. All absences not reported to the school will be recorded as unauthorised, until the reason for your child not being at school is established.
Sickness
Please report your child’s absence in by using the following email address absent@newkings.q1e.org.uk or by telephone to the School Office on 020 7736 2318 before 9.00am. Please refer to National Health Service guidance if you are unsure whether your child should remain at home.
